key_insight: Stronger teacher reasoning traces don’t always produce better student reasoners; instead, selecting trajectories by how informatively they align with a student model better predicts which examples will teach the student to reason. The paper proposes a simple "informative alignment" metric to quantify this suitability.
problem_solved: Distillation of chain-of-thought reasoning from teacher to student LLMs often fails because existing selection criteria (e.g., student likelihood) prefer trajectories that merely match the student's current behavior rather than ones that drive learning; this work addresses how to choose trajectories that actually improve student reasoning.
method: Define a simple informative-alignment metric that captures how a teacher trajectory both aligns with and adds learning signal relative to the student.
Score and rank teacher CoT trajectories using this metric instead of relying solely on student likelihood or teacher strength.
Select high-scoring trajectories for distillation and validate that these choices better predict student learning outcomes (empirical evaluation).
impact: Provides a practical, data-driven way to choose reasoning trajectories for distillation, improving efficiency and effectiveness of teaching student LLMs without requiring larger or stronger teachers. Practitioners can get better student reasoning by prioritizing informative alignment over raw teacher quality.
visual_elements: Flow diagram: Teacher trajectories → Informative alignment metric → Selected trajectories → Student model (distillation pipeline).
Bar chart: Comparison of student performance when trained on (a) strongest-teacher trajectories vs (b) informative-alignment-selected trajectories.
Heatmap or scatter: Trajectories plotted by student-likelihood vs informative-alignment score to show selection differences.
Icon set: teacher (brain/robot), student (smaller robot), magnifying glass (metric), upward arrow (improvement)
paper_title: Which Reasoning Trajectories Teach Students to Reason Better? A Simple Metric of Informative Alignment
paper_authors: Yuming Yang, Mingyoung Lai, Wanxu Zhao, Xiaoran Fan, Zhiheng Xi
